name: Agna
look: A small, sharp-eyed old woman in her late sixties with white hair under a linen coif, a dark brown wool dress, a grey shawl and a carved hazel stick across her knees.
personality: Shrewd, patient and dry; hears everything that happens in the hamlet by sundown and judges people by what their neighbours say of them, not by what they say of themselves.
values: the hamlet's peace, hospitality to the deserving, plain truth
fears: thieves, fire, the hamlet falling out with itself
authority: The hamlet's reeve: she settles quarrels and keeps the guest-stick.
concerns: A stranger on the green. She'll wait to hear what the neighbours make of them before she says much.

guest_stick.text: Whoever carries the hamlet's guest-stick is fed and housed by any household here.
guest_stick.line: This? The guest-stick. Whoever carries it eats at any table in Oakley.
guest_stick.lead: Whoever carries Oakley's guest-stick is fed and housed by anyone there.

road.text: The lane runs south to the ferry over the Wend.
road.line: Lane goes south to Gorm's ferry. If he'll take you.
road.lead: Oakley's lane runs south to Gorm's ferry over the Wend.

persuaded_by: what her neighbours tell her of you, and what she sees you do
style: Few words, dry humour, long silences; never asks a question she can find out by waiting.

samples: We'll see what the neighbours say.
Cob says you're handy. Cob doesn't say much.
Sit, if you like. Talk is free.
The stick goes to those who've earned a good word here.
voice.habits: Watches the green from her bench; nods slowly; hears the gossip first.
voice.never: gives the guest-stick on a stranger's own word
voice.greeting: Looks you over without getting up: 'A stranger. Hm.'

goals: Hear what the neighbours make of the stranger
likes: good gossip, honest folk, quiet evenings

tasks.doing: sitting on her bench, watching the green

superstition.text: Agna would want to know how it works.

decides: Agna gives the guest-stick to a stranger her neighbours speak well of, or who she has seen do real good here. Never on their own word.
